text.p: Telecommunications and systems integrator Datacraft Ltd said on Tuesday it expected further performance improvements in the year to June 30, 1998 after a return to profitability in 1996/97.
"We anticipate further improvement in performance across the group in the coming year," Datacraft said in a statement accompanying its annual results.
Earlier, Datacraft reported a net profit of A$6.91 million in 1996/97, compared with a loss of A$8.89 million a year earlier, while total revenue rose 41.2 percent to A$277.8 million in the year.
Datacraft said the local businesses are now restructured. The Asian business would be expanding regionally into new markets as well as within countries where it already operated.
In a rapidly developing market, the Latin American business started the year with a strong backlog, Datacraft said.
Datacraft Asia Ltd, about 55 percent owned by Datacraft Ltd, reported on Monday a 54.8 percent increase in net profit to US$10.34 million in the year to June 30, 1997.
Datacraft Ltd said its profit turnaround was due to a return to profitability locally, a madien profit in the Americas in its second full year of operations and strong growth in Asia.

"Datacraft's market opportunity continues to look very positive with the deregulation of carrier business, the rapid expansion of the Internet and the demand by corporates for data communication, networks and services," Datacraft said.

Rapid expansion of infrastructure throughout Asia continues to fuel Datacraft Asia's growth. Allied to this, the focus on growth in the services segment would ensure that profitability levels are maintained, it said.
"Asia's revenues and profits are expected to continue growing at a rapid rate during 1997/98," the Australian company said.
"In Brazil, Datacraft Americas is seeking to replicate the outstanding success of Datacraft Asia at a time when the Brasilian communications industry is deregulating and privatising," Datacraft said.
"Every indication is that the current growth will continue for the foreseeable future in both (Asian and Latin America) regions," it said.

"While the company continues to address its profitability in Australia, its overseas operations are targeted at major markets where it is achieving exceptional results and which offer enormous opportunities for long term growth," it said.
At 10.40 a.m. (0040 GMT), Datacraft shares were 20 cents higher at A$2.65 in light trade.
